technique_why: A sky, far hills, a near hillside and a field with one animal in front: paint-along, back to front, on a white canvas is the beginner approach that fits, with the cow and the grass in front of it last.
subject: A shaggy ginger Highland cow standing in tall summer grass on a hillside at sunset, with blue-violet mountains, a sliver of loch and a gold and blue sky behind it
focal_point: The cow's face: the pink-brown nose and the golden fringe falling over the eyes, with the horns curving up on either side
light: A low setting sun from the right and slightly behind the cow, so the sky is brightest low on the right, the top of the head, the fringe and the cow's right-hand edge glow with a gold rim, the left and front of the coat fall into shadow, and the grass tips catch gold
why: Paint the scene back to front on white: the sky straight through, then the mountains and loch, then one blended green ground that runs behind where the cow will stand. The cow is built as a shape, shaded, given its horns, then its locks are pulled down in two lighter passes and the sun's rim is laid on hair and horns together, before the face. The tall grass goes on last, over the cow's legs, in passes from dark to gold, so most of the steps go to the cow and the grass in front.

things.name: The sunset sky
things.why: A smooth gradient from soft blue at the top to pale gold and apricot low on the right, blended wet in one go.

things.name: The gold cloud streaks
things.why: Thin, soft streaks laid on the dry sky with a nearly dry brush, then lit on their top edges.
things.left_out: The brightest white edges (the clouds' optional third step): these are thin far streaks, and a gold top edge is enough.

things.name: The blue-violet mountains
things.why: Far ranges as big flat shapes, the farthest palest and the nearer ridge darker and bluer.
things.left_out: Separate shadow and light sides on the ranges: in the finish they are two flat values, and a beginner keeps far hills simple.

things.name: The sliver of loch
things.why: A small strip of water seen past the slope on the right, one pale horizontal lay-in.
things.left_out: Ripples and lighter streaks: the strip is too small and far for them.

things.name: The green hillside behind the cow
things.why: The rolling slope between the mountains and the cow, a field laid in lighter and yellower toward the sun.

things.name: The dark bushes on the hillside
things.why: The dark green clumps dappled over the slope read as low bushes: dark dabs first, then a few sunlit taps.
things.left_out: The middle-value leaves (foliage's optional middle step): the hillside green under them already plays the middle value.
things.plain: the dark bush clumps, with no light on them

things.name: The tall grass in front
things.why: Foreground grass: a dark green base, then flicked blades from dark to gold over it and over the cow's legs.
things.left_out: The seed heads and single fine stalks in the photo: a beginner makes the grass from flicked blades only.
things.plain: the plain green meadow, smooth, with no grass blades

things.name: The Highland cow
things.why: A long-haired animal whose coat hangs in locks, exactly what this element is for: shape, shadow, locks, lit rim, face.
things.left_out: A painted eye: in the finish the eyes are hidden under the fringe, so only a dark touch shows where one peeks out. The legs and hooves are lost in the grass.

things.name: The horns
things.why: Two curved tapering shapes built from pieces, shaded underneath and lit on top.

paints.name: Warm apricot

paints.name: Pale lavender-white

paints.looks: a warm, light yellow-green, grass where the sun hits

paints.name: Olive green
paints.looks: a mid, slightly dull olive green, the body of the grass

paints.name: Deep grass green
paints.looks: a dark, cool blue-green, the bushes and the shadows in the grass

paints.looks: a warm mid red-brown, the main color of the cow's coat

steps.name: Blend the sunset sky

lays.what: the whole sky: soft blue across the top, easing into pale gold through the middle and warm apricot low on the right where the sun is, run down past the mountain line to about the middle of the canvas

steps.after: The top half of the canvas is a smooth sky, blue at the top, gold in the middle and glowing apricot low on the right; its colors run a little past where the mountains will go. The bottom half is bare white.
steps.why: The farthest thing goes first, and it runs past the horizon so nothing has to be painted around.

steps.name: Dry-brush the cloud streaks

lays.what: long thin streaks across the sky: apricot streaks low and toward the right, a few hazy blue-violet streaks higher on the left as the shadowed undersides

steps.after: Soft, broken horizontal cloud streaks lie over the dry sky, apricot near the sun and grayish violet higher up, with the sky showing through their edges. Their tops are not yet lit. Below the middle is still bare.

steps.name: Light the tops of the clouds

lays.what: a thin pale gold edge along the top of each streak, more on the streaks nearest the sun on the right

steps.after: Each cloud streak now has a glowing gold top edge, with its darker apricot or violet still showing underneath. The sky is finished; the lower half is bare.

steps.name: Lay in the mountain ranges

lays.what: the farthest range in hazy blue-violet along the horizon, then the nearer, lower ridge overlapping it in deep slate blue, sloping down toward the right

steps.after: A band of soft mountains crosses the canvas just above the middle: a pale blue-violet far range with a darker blue ridge in front of it. No texture. Below them the canvas is still white, with sky color showing at the top edge of the white.
steps.why: Back to front: the mountains overlap the sky, the nearer ridge overlaps the far range.

steps.name: Streak in the loch

lays.what: a short, thin pale strip of water at the right edge, tucked under the nearer ridge

steps.after: A small pale sliver of loch shines at the right edge under the dark ridge. Everything below the mountains is still bare.

stages.name: The green slope and the meadow

steps.name: Lay in the hillside and the meadow

lays.what: the rolling slope just under the mountains, sunlit yellow-green blending into olive green, sloping down from left to right
the whole lower half of the canvas, olive green blending down into deep grass green at the bottom edge, straight through where the cow will stand

steps.after: The whole bottom half is covered in green: lighter and yellower just under the mountains, olive through the middle, dark green at the bottom. It is smooth, with no bushes, blades or cow yet.
steps.why: One loaded brush blends the ground from back to front in one go; the cow is painted over it.

steps.name: Dab the dark bushes on the hillside

lays.what: scattered dark clumps across the hillside, in loose rows that follow the slope, smaller and closer together toward the mountains

steps.after: The hillside is dappled with dark green clumps in rows that follow the slope, with the lighter green showing between them. The meadow below and where the cow goes are unchanged.

steps.name: Tap the sun on the bushes

lays.what: a few light taps on the right-hand, sunward tops of the clumps

steps.after: The tops of the bushes on the sun side catch yellow-green light, with most of each clump still dark. The background is finished; the cow's place is still plain green.

steps.name: Block in the cow

lays.what: the whole cow in rust brown: a big tall oval for the body left of center, the head as a smaller rounded shape to the upper right of it, a curved cap for the fringe over the head, an ear on each side, and short pieces for the legs going down into the grass, every stroke curving down the way the hair hangs

steps.after: A flat rust-brown cow shape stands over the green: body, head, fringe and ears, legs fading into the meadow. No horns, no shadow, no locks, no face yet.
steps.why: Big shape first, built from simple pieces, before any shading or hair.

steps.name: Shade the cow's shadow side

lays.what: long downward curves of deep red-brown on the left and front of the body, under the head and the fringe, down the chest and low on the belly and legs, leaving the rust showing on the sun side to the right

steps.after: The cow has a dark side: the left of the body, the chest, under the chin and under the fringe are deep red-brown, the right side still flat rust. It looks rounded but still smooth, with no locks.

steps.name: Block in the horns

lays.what: the two horns in horn taupe, each built as a thick piece at the head and curving pieces that taper upward: the left horn sweeps up high, the right one curves out and up

steps.after: Two flat grayish-tan horns curve up from either side of the head, over the hillside and mountains. They have no shading yet.
steps.why: The horns go on before the locks so the fringe can fall over their bases.

steps.name: Shade the undersides of the horns

lays.what: deep red-brown along the underside of each horn's curve, at its base by the head and darker toward the tips

steps.after: Each horn has a dark underside and darker tip, the taupe showing along the top. The horns look round but are not yet lit.

steps.name: Pull the copper locks

lays.what: long tapering locks of copper orange hanging down over the body, the head and the fringe, following the body's curve, with gaps so the darker coat shows, fewer on the shadow side; the fringe locks fall over the bases of the horns

steps.after: The cow's coat now hangs in copper locks over the dark and rust base, which still shows in the gaps, most of all on the left. The fringe covers the eyes and the horn bases. No gold yet.
steps.why: The locks build lighter over the dry shaded base, darkest first.

steps.name: Pull the sunlit golden locks

lays.what: fewer, shorter golden locks over the copper, on the top of the head, the fringe and the right side of the body and chest that face the sun

steps.after: Gold locks glow on the fringe, the top of the head and the sun side of the cow, covering less than the copper; the left side stays mostly copper and dark. The coat looks shaggy but has no bright rim yet.

steps.name: Catch the sun's rim on the hair and horns

lays.what: short broken pale gold touches running off the edges that face the sun: the top of the fringe, the right ear and cheek, and the right-hand outline of the chest and body
a thin pale gold light along the top edge of each horn's curve

steps.after: A glowing pale gold rim outlines the cow on the sun side and along the top of the fringe, and the tops of both horns are lit; the darker locks show through the broken strokes. Light over dark may need a second thin coat once dry. The face is still unpainted.
steps.why: The same low sun lights the hair and the horns: one brush of pale gold, dry-brushed along every edge that faces it.

steps.name: Paint the nose

lays.what: the broad muzzle under the fringe, a rounded shape in rosy brown, wider at the bottom

steps.after: A rounded pink-brown nose sits under the fringe on the right of the head. It has no nostrils, no light and no mouth yet.

steps.name: Light the top of the nose

lays.what: a small curved touch of pale rose across the top of the nose, on the sun side

steps.after: The top of the nose is lit pale pink, with the rosy brown still showing around and below it. Still no nostrils or mouth.

steps.name: Dot the nostrils and the eye

lays.what: two dark nostrils on the front of the nose, and a small dark touch where the left eye peeks out under the fringe

steps.after: The nose has two dark nostrils and a dark eye shows under the fringe to the left of the nose. The mouth line is not there yet.

steps.name: Line the mouth and chin

lays.what: a short curved mouth line under the nose and a thin dark line under the chin

steps.after: The face is finished: nose, nostrils, the hint of an eye and a mouth line. The cow's legs and lower body still sit on plain green with no grass in front.

steps.name: Flick the dark grass blades

lays.what: dark green blades flicked up all over the meadow and over the cow's lower legs and belly, so the cow stands in the grass, longest at the bottom of the canvas

steps.after: Dark blades cover the meadow and hide the cow's legs and the bottom of its belly. The grass reads as dark and dense, with no light blades yet.
steps.why: What's in front of the subject goes on after it, darkest marks first.

steps.name: Flick the olive blades

lays.what: olive green blades over most of the meadow, including over the cow's lower legs, leaving the dark blades showing between them

steps.after: The meadow has olive blades over the dark ones, so the grass has depth; the dark still shows between them. It is still all green, with no gold.

steps.name: Flick the sunlit green blades

lays.what: fewer yellow-green blades, more toward the right where the sun is and across the upper meadow

steps.after: Sunlit yellow-green blades lighten the meadow toward the right and the top, covering less than the olive. No gold blades yet.

steps.name: Flick the golden blades

lays.what: scattered gold blades, larger and farther apart at the bottom, smaller and closer up the meadow, some crossing in front of the cow's legs and belly

steps.after: Gold blades catch the sun all over the meadow and in front of the cow, with the greens showing between them. Only the brightest tips are missing.

steps.name: Flick the brightest grass tips

lays.what: a few pale gold flicks on the tips of the tallest gold blades, mostly on the sun side and in front of the cow

steps.after: The finished painting: a few blade tips glow pale gold in the foreground, the brightest touches in the grass, matching the gold rim on the cow.
steps.why: The last step is the brightest highlights.
